packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-13 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind; no outside source consulted, no identification attempted)

Images viewed: image-001 to image-026 (all that exist; 027 and 028 are not present).
image-001 = overview of side A (with colour chart); image-002..013 = details of side A.
image-014 = overview of side B; image-015..026 = details of side B.

Exposure statement: the images themselves show a modern ink stamp of a library and a pencilled
shelf-mark ("Fragm. 102") in the lower margin of side A, a pencilled "3604"(?) at lower left and a
pencilled "1" at upper right. I could not avoid seeing these. They say nothing about the text
and I did not use them. No other outside information was used.

====================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
====================================================================
- One parchment sheet, landscape, with a vertical fold/gutter down the middle and sewing holes
  along it: a bifolium laid open. Each half carries TWO narrow columns, so four columns are
  visible on each side. I label them col. 1-4 from left to right on each side. Because this is
  a bifolium, col. 1-2 and col. 3-4 belong to two different leaves; the text need not run on
  from col. 2 to col. 3 (uncertain column order across the fold).
- Lower right corner cut away diagonally (side A) / lower left (side B); wide blank lower
  margin; trimmed close at the top (side A top lines are right at the edge).
- Script: small, compressed, cursive-influenced bookhand in pale brown ink, c. 33-36 lines per
  column, ruled lines visible. Heavily abbreviated.
- No running titles seen. No colour: no red or blue anywhere on the leaf (observation).
- Articulation: every so often a short line is INDENTED and followed by a second indented line,
  the first of them usually with a slightly larger initial; a blank space is left at the left,
  presumably for an initial that was never supplied (tentative). These look like headings /
  openings of successive short units. I count such openings at: side A col. 1 near the top
  (image-002 L2), col. 2 lower third (image-007 L3) and last line (image-011), col. 3 (image-004
  L5), col. 4 (image-005 L3 and image-009 L13); side B col. 2 (image-016 c. L13), col. 3
  (image-021 L4, L14, image-025 L5), col. 4 (image-022 L5, L20, L22).
- A small marginal sign (like "⁊" or "c") stands in the intercolumn beside the heading in side A
  col. 2 (image-007 L3) and beside side B col. 3 heading (image-021 L4).
- No interlinear gloss or commentary layer; single text block per column.
- Tentative interpretation only: the vocabulary (salutem, uxor, marito, dilectio, soror, nepotes,
  notario, scolares, littere) and the short units with indented openings suggest a series of
  short letter-like pieces. I do not infer a work or author.
- Condition: side A is much the more legible; the upper quarter of every column on both sides is
  rubbed/stained and holed; side B is faint over most of col. 1 lower half, col. 2 top, col. 3
  top half.

Selected for reading: side A col. 1 (upper and lower), col. 2 (middle and the unit beginning in
the lower third), col. 3 (from the heading down), col. 4 (most of it); side B: openings and the
better-preserved stretches of col. 1, 2, 3, 4. Unread / not resolved: the top 6-8 lines of each
column on side A as seen only in the overview (no detail image covers the very top of side A);
most of side B col. 1 lower half and col. 3 upper half.

Conventions: ( ) = proposed expansion; ? after a word = uncertain; ?? = little more than a guess
at letter shapes; [illegible]; [hole]; lines are physical lines; numbering is counted from the
top of the named image, counting partly visible lines, and may be off by one where the top line
is clipped.

4. LIMITATIONS
====================================================================
- This is a low-confidence reading. The hand is small and cursive, the ink pale, and the
  detail images are only moderately sharp at letter level; minims (n/u/m/i) are frequently
  indistinguishable and many abbreviation strokes are lost. Words marked ?? should not be used
  as match evidence on their own. The best anchors are the strings listed at the end of
  section 2 and, on side B, "ad id efficiendum", "filios castigate(?) non filii suos patres"
  and the recurring scolar-/stud-/legend- vocabulary in col. 2.
- No detail image covers the top 6-8 lines of the four columns of side A (image-002 to 005
  begin lower); those lines are visible only in the reduced overview and were not transcribed.
  A crop of the top strip of side A would be the single most useful addition.
- The upper quarter of all columns on both sides is abraded, stained and holed.
- Headings/unit openings were left without their initials (blank indents), so first letters of
  several units are not on the page; I did not supply them.
- Column order across the central fold is not assured (bifolium); which side is recto/verso
  and whether the two leaves were consecutive cannot be told from the images.
- Line numbers may be off by one where the first line of a crop is clipped.
- Nothing was supplied from memory of any specific text; no source was consulted.
